principle: REGISTRY ONTOLOGY — the registry-of-registries. Owner vision (2026-06-23): Teleon is not 'an agent framework' but a machine-readable model of all executable capability — a FEDERATION of knowledge registries each behind ONE universal interface (the Bloomberg-Terminal-of-computation shape). This file indexes the load-bearing registries, maps each to its REAL backing module/file + the Open*Hub that exposes it + the compiler stage it serves, and marks status live|partial|gap so the model understands the SCALE and the DIRECTORIES it pulls from. Finer layer beneath hub_profiles.json (a hub can expose several registries). serves_truth=false (an ontology of pointers/shapes, never truth or a data dump). Anti-drift: every live/partial backing path is existence-checked by scripts/check_registry_ontology.py.

context.repo_already_has: ~180 architecture/*.json registries + 48 src/teleon submodules + 45 schemas/ subdirs — the federation is largely ALREADY INSTANTIATED; the work is (a) one universal interface so they are ONE governed pattern, and (b) filling the ~6 real gaps, NOT hand-building 35 new catalogs.
context.naming: Use 'registry' for a structured knowledge layer about computation; 'hub' for the Open*Hub surface that exposes one or more registries. A registry is finer than a hub.

consumption_model.note: The registries are a BUFFET (owner framing 2026-06-23): tools / knowledge / strategies / sources / standards an AI AGENT (the customer) CONSUMES to assemble a functional, VALUE-ADD DAG. Supply = these registries; the MENU = the universal Registry<T> interface (search/lookup/score/benchmark); demand = agents building DAGs via the synthesis compiler. An agent does NOT hand-write a DAG — it PICKS ingredients from the buffet under its constraints, then the compiler composes + verifies + optimizes. This is the DEMAND side of the ontology; the layers/kinds above are the SUPPLY side.
flow: PICK: search the registries for ingredients (capability #1 -> component #2 -> model/provider #4/#5 -> source/lookup #31/#72/#77 -> strategy/heuristic #13 -> validator #36)
COMPOSE: the synthesis compiler assembles a DAG from the picked components
VERIFY: verify_buildable_dag + validation #36 — the DAG is buildable + value-add
OPTIMIZE: the descent prunes to cheapest-deterministic (optimization_pass #10)
EXECUTE + MEASURE: run, emit receipts, feed the flywheel (execution_memory #29, experiment #49)
consumption_model.agents_are_customers: Per the agent-capability-gateway thesis: agents call stable receipt-backed capabilities instead of burning tokens re-deriving them. A value-add DAG = cheaper + verified vs the agent doing it blind. The buffet is what they call; a registry that no DAG-builder reads is dead weight (the sequencing law).

engines.note: Three super-systems (owner framing 2026-06-23): (1) DISCOVERY ENGINE — search the world for computation (Layer 0 + discovery_subsystem); (2) COMPILER ENGINE — build the optimal verified execution DAG (synthesis -> dag -> descent, the consumption_model flow); (3) INTELLIGENCE ENGINE — understand the world's operational infrastructure (the registries + the RegistryPort menu + the dependency-graph meta-registry #83). Google indexes documents; Teleon indexes CAPABILITY — what machines / systems / agents / APIs / portals / workflows / data can do. A universal index of machine-actionable civilization.
engines.discovery_engine: Layer 0 discovery registries + discovery_subsystem (search the world for computation)
engines.compiler_engine: synthesis -> dag -> descent (build the optimal verified DAG)
engines.intelligence_engine: the registries + the RegistryPort menu + the #83 dependency-graph meta-registry (understand the operational infrastructure)

universal_interface.note: Owner-proposed Registry<T> contract: every registry SHOULD expose these verbs behind one agnostic port (single source of truth, like makeHub(config)). Most verbs already have a backing primitive in-repo (named); the gap is a SINGLE declared contract all registries conform to.
universal_interface.interface_status: DECLARED + conformant: src/teleon/registry/port.py = the RegistryPort menu (list/lookup/search/explain) over 7 source catalogs (lookup_portals/observability/geospatial/vulnerability/knowledge_taxonomies/human_expert/semantic), proven uniform by check_registry_port; remaining verbs (benchmark/score/health/relationships/history/mutate/simulate) wire to their named primitives next + more catalogs join the menu

universal_object.note: Owner-proposed RegistryObject shape every entry inherits (Models, APIs, Providers, Templates, Datasets, Adapters, Policies, Prompts — identical shape). ANTI-FRAGMENTATION: the rigid shape is a real JSON Schema (single source of truth), not just this list — owner's #1 risk is ontology fragmentation, so the schema is enforced, not aspirational.

universes.note: The layered model (owner architectural shift 2026-06-23): every registry belongs to exactly ONE universe. Membership is single-sourced HERE as id-lists (NOT duplicated per-entry) so it can't fragment; check_registry_ontology enforces a clean partition over every registry id. Layer 0 (Discovery) is the supply-chain INTAKE layer that continuously maps the external world and FEEDS Layers 1-4 (the 4 core universes). Layers 1-3 are heavily modeled; Layer 4 (Verification) is the underbuilt moat layer.

layer0_discovery.label: Discovery Universe — continuously map the external computational supply chain (the search engine for global machine capability); feeds all other layers

layer1_capability.label: Capability Universe — what computation can do

layer2_execution.label: Execution Universe — what components/models/APIs/providers/systems (incl. human labor) execute it

layer3_optimization.label: Optimization Universe — make execution cheaper/faster/more deterministic

layer4_verification.label: Verification Universe — know execution was correct + continuously improve (the underbuilt moat)

registry_kinds.note: Owner shift (2026-06-23): STATIC registry (curated, already indexed) vs DISCOVERY registry (continuously crawls the world for new components) vs META registry (knows WHERE public registries are; stores POINTERS, never content — fetch on demand). Single-sourced id-lists, partition-checked. META is the GOVERNANCE-CORRECT DEFAULT for external sources: pointer != copy, discovery != trust, no data dump (CLAUDE.md: don't republish _reference). The 3-tier substrate already exists in architecture/registry_layers.json (core_curated | staged_massive | feeds).

discovery.label: crawler + benchmark + intelligence (continuously discovers external resources)

meta.label: pointer-only index of external registries + lookup portals + human-labor marketplaces + geo/vuln source feeds; stores no content (the keystone answer to 'registries that know where to look things up')

boundaries.note: Overlap-resolution rules (owner: 'avoid overlap and redundancy'). SINGLE SOURCE for the boundary between adjacent registries so none is redundant. Two orthogonal axes already separate most: UNIVERSE (what it's ABOUT) x KIND (static=curated | discovery=crawls | meta=pointer-only). These rules disambiguate the rest:
boundaries.discovery_feeds_static: a DISCOVERY registry (56-68, 73) CRAWLS/streams an external source for NEW items; its CURATED counterpart holds the promoted, scored subset. Pairs: 56->12 dataset, 57->4 model, 58+66->2 component, 60->3 api_endpoint, 61->37 benchmark, 63->5 provider. Discovery FEEDS static across the staged_massive promotion boundary (registry_layers.json) — not redundant, it is the intake stage of the same pipeline.
boundaries.package_vs_repo: 58 package_discovery = published PACKAGES (PyPI/npm/crates artifacts); 66 repo_discovery = source REPOS (GitHub/GitLab + maintainer signals). Overlap only on GitHub.
boundaries.meta_kinds: META registries store POINTERS, never content, differentiated by WHAT they point at: 69 external_registry_index -> where other REGISTRIES live; 72 lookup_portals -> where to look up a single FACT (license/weather/property); 74 human_expert_sources -> where to get HUMAN labor; 73 feed_sources (discovery kind) -> PUSH feeds pulled on a cadence.
boundaries.systems_vs_parts: by HOW you use it: 70 agent_systems = autonomous AGENTS that do end-to-end work; 71 external_systems = SaaS/tools/infra you ACT INSIDE; 2 component = libraries you CALL; 31 data_source = systems you READ FROM; 74 human_expert_sources = HUMANS you route work to.
boundaries.verification_pairs: 7 failure = failure MODES (what breaks + frequency) vs 52 failure_recovery = recovery TREES (what to do next). 14 agent_behavior = how agents behave in general vs 46 agent_qa = per-run agent quality/waste metrics. 23 security = code/package VULNERABILITIES (CVE) vs 24 trust = REPUTATION score. 12 dataset = existing corpora vs 42 synthetic_data = GENERATED edge cases. 27 human_approval = internal approval RULES vs 74 human_expert_sources = external human LABOR.

discovery_subsystem.note: Owner-proposed (2026-06-23) discovery.aidoneright.com — a subsystem ABOVE all registries: Internet -> continuous crawlers -> classifiers -> benchmark harnesses -> security/license audit -> metadata extraction -> registry population -> compiler availability; tracks changes + removes deprecated. Framing: NOT 'we have registries' but 'we are the search engine for global machine capability' (Google indexes documents; Teleon indexes executable computation). Already partly built + PROVEN-LIVE.
discovery_subsystem.governance: discovery != trust; crawled items are CANDIDATES in the staged_massive tier (registry_layers.json), NOT read until promoted past the license-gated promotion boundary; never republish source content (store pointers + metadata only).
discovery_subsystem.owner_gated: discovery.aidoneright.com as a public subdomain needs owner domain/trademark clearance (recorded as proposed, not claimed).

rules: Schema-all-now, fill-gap-first: declaring the ontology of every registry is cheap and makes the scale legible (this file). FILLING a registry is expensive and only pays when the descent/compiler PRUNES on it.
A registry nothing reads is dead weight: stand a registry up when a real pipeline needs it, proven on the STARTER vertical (HealthLynked provider directory), not speculatively.

Moat = the FLYWHEEL that fills + scores these registries from real runs, NOT the registry count. A wall of empty catalogs is not a moat. The owner names Layer 4 (Verification) as the likely moat — invest there.

Universal interface BEFORE more registries: one declared Registry<T> contract + RegistryObject base shape turns ~180 existing JSONs into one governed pattern — higher leverage than any single new registry.

Highest-leverage gaps to stand up first (owner-flagged as moat/huge): failure (7), equivalence (11), semantic_ontology (20); then cost forecasting (15) + agent_behavior (14) when agents-as-customers lands.
